source.title: UP-DOWN cortical dynamics reflect state transitions in a bistable network

confidence_rationale: Good source: eLife, a model that makes a non-obvious falsifiable prediction (inhibitory rates should decay markedly within UP states while excitatory rates barely do) which the authors then confirm in rat recordings. Mapping fidelity is high on ARCHITECTURAL FORM -- this is the cleanest worked example of the exact hybrid the SalienceCoordinator implements -- but the biological content is spontaneous cortical dynamics under anaesthesia, which is several removes from mode arbitration in a behaving agent. Direction is mixed because the paper supports one half of MECH-019 and supplies the mechanism for the other half.
failure_signatures: A network whose control parameter varies continuously can still produce state transitions that are genuinely discrete and fluctuation-triggered, with no graded precursor in the state variable itself -- the gradedness lives in the transition RATE, not in the trajectory.
DOWN-to-UP transitions required synchronous high-amplitude events, i.e. they were driven by noise crossing a threshold rather than by the control parameter smoothly carrying the state across.

Bistability implies hysteresis, so occupancy measured during an up-sweep and a down-sweep of the same channel will not coincide; a single-direction sweep cannot distinguish graded shaping from a hysteretic switch.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Spontaneous UP and DOWN cortical population states in anaesthetised rat are not generated by a rhythmic oscillator but by a BISTABLE excitatory-inhibitory network in which both states are attractors and transitions between them are triggered by fluctuations; UP and DOWN durations are highly variable, population rate does not decay appreciably within UP periods in excitatory cells, and -- as the model uniquely predicts and the recordings confirm -- inhibitory cell rates DO decay markedly within UP periods. DOWN-to-UP transitions required synchronous high-amplitude events.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the architectural form the SalienceCoordinator actually has, described exactly. Continuous channels set affinity weights (the control parameter); the system occupies discrete attractor-like modes; mode_switch_trigger fires on a MECH-259 threshold crossing; and exit_thresholds impose hysteresis, which is the computational signature of bistability. Jercog et al. show that such a system is correctly described BOTH as continuously shaped (the control parameter smoothly sets dwell times and transition rates) AND as discretely switching (the state variable itself jumps, driven by noise). MECH-019 and its own FALSIFYING criterion are, on this reading, describing the same architecture at two different levels.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The preparation is spontaneous activity in anaesthetised rat cortex -- no task, no behaviour, no mode arbitration, and an anaesthetic regime that is known to exaggerate bistability relative to the awake state. The mapping is therefore to DYNAMICAL ARCHITECTURE, not to cognitive mode selection, and should not be read as evidence that REE's four operating modes are attractors in the same sense. Its value is that it supplies a concrete, well-characterised counterexample to the assumption that 'continuously shaped' and 'discretely switching' are alternatives.
mapping.source_context: Anaesthetised rats; extracellular multi-unit and single-unit population recordings of spontaneous cortical activity, analysed against a rate model with separate excitatory and inhibitory populations plus adaptation, and a spiking network implementation.

confidence_components.notes: mapping_fidelity is relatively high for an animal-physiology paper because what is being transferred is a dynamical-systems architecture rather than a biological mechanism, and the substrate demonstrably has that architecture (softmax over modes + threshold trigger + exit-threshold hysteresis). transfer_risk 0.40 is the highest in this pull, driven by anaesthesia and by the absence of any behavioural or cognitive content in the preparation.
